The text contains several specific historical markers that pinpoint its time period. The most definitive clue is the mention of the "ratification of the 18th Amendment." The 18th Amendment to the United States Constitution, which established the prohibition of alcohol, was ratified on January 16, 1919, and went into effect on January 17, 1920.

Additionally, the context of a pamphlet advocating for sobriety and opposing the "liquor trade" aligns with the era of Prohibition in the United States, which lasted from 1920 to 1933. The reference to the drink coming from cows (milk) serves as a contrast to the prohibited alcohol, a common theme in temperance literature of that time.

Therefore, the text dates to the early 1920s, specifically around the time of the ratification and enforcement of Prohibition.

Answer: Early 1920s (specifically circa 1919–1920)
